Discussed catalog differences, quantization variants, and rollback mechanics. Agreed to run a 48h A/B with clear pass criteria and to share an annotated comparison matrix.
transcript:
Header: 2025-09-02 16:23 PDT | Duration 47m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Moreno (SE), Hannah Park (CSM); Priya Nair, Tomás Alvarez, Sofia Berg, Jake (NimbleRetail)

Summary: quick sync on chosen model variants, how we pin in catalog, and the fallback behavior for degraded infra or cost pressures. Plan to run 48h A/B test with pinned versions and soft fallback rules.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, we left off last week with the candidate set and some initial perf numbers so today we want to prioritize pinning a default and a fallback plus the canary plan.
[00:18] Priya Nair: yep, thanks. Quick note — our product team wants a deterministic rollback path, they don't want surprises during peak.
[00:28] Luis Moreno: Totally, so the idea is we set a "primary" pin and a lighter fallback pin, and use the soft-fallback policy where we only route if latency or error budget crosses threshold, we can tune thresholds.
[00:45] Tomás Alvarez: Can you remind me which exact model names we're comparing? The internal names confused me last time.
[00:54] Avery Chen: Sure — in the catalog we have the 1) nimble-red-3-35b-q4 (our quantized candidate), 2) open-llm-70b-fp16 (large non-quant), and 3) red-chat-3.1-13b-q4 as the smaller fallback. I'll send the matrix after the call.
[01:15] Priya Nair: Right, the 35b quant looked good on quality for our prompts but the P95 was flirting with 240ms in our regional tests, which is higher than their SLO.
[01:32] Jake: also saw token cost delta — the 35b quant is about $1.10 per 1k tokens in our rough calc vs 0.36 for the 13b q4.
[01:45] Sofia Berg: so the tradeoff is cost vs quality, and when do we fallback. What is a soft fallback exactly?
[01:55] Luis Moreno: Soft fallback means we attempt the primary, but if we hit a latency or error threshold we automatically route that single request to the fallback model. It's not a full switch — it's per-request reroute and we tag telemetry so you see why each request fell back.
[02:13] Priya Nair: I like tagging, that's important for regressions. Will it preserve the conversation KV cache? Because we rely on long chat context.
[02:27] Luis Moreno: Good call — the KV cache is model-specific. If we fallback to a smaller arch that doesn't share compatible KV encoding, we replay the last N tokens into the fallback request. There's a small latency hit for that replay but it's accounted for. We can configure prefix/KV cache policy to reduce replay length.
[02:46] Tomás Alvarez: We need the exact expected penalty numbers, otherwise ops will panic. Do you have example numbers?
[02:56] Avery Chen: From our internal bench, KV replay for a 2k token context adds roughly 50-90ms on GPU workloads depending on kernel path. We'll add those to the matrix.
[03:10] Sofia Berg: Ok. Regarding pinning — can we pin to quantized build vs floating point build? Are those two separate pins?
[03:20] Luis Moreno: Yes, pins are per model variant. So you can pin nimble-red-3-35b-q4 or nimble-red-3-35b-fp16. Pins also encode which compilation profile and quantization artifact to use, so rollback to earlier pin is straightforward.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Is there a way to do staged rollouts? Like 1% then 10% then full?
[03:43] Avery Chen: Absolutely — Redwood rollout supports percentage-based canaries and automatic ramp if pass conditions are met. We'll configure a 5/25/100 ramp unless you want different.
[03:53] Tomás Alvarez: Our telemetry hooks — we need to surface p95 latency, error rate, hallucination score (approx), and token cost per request. Can Redwood export those as custom metrics?
[04:06] Luis Moreno: Yes, we emit token_cost, gpu_ms, p50/p95/p99 latency, and you can send hallucination flags via our quality hook. We'll make sure the pilot namespace has the tags you need.
[04:21] Priya Nair: On the catalog comparison — you mentioned the 70b fp16 variant, is that an in-house model or third-party? We want to know licensing and data residency implications.
[04:33] Avery Chen: The open-llm-70b-fp16 is community licensed; we noted the license in the matrix. For data residency we'd recommend private deployment if you need on-prem; otherwise hosted with our region controls is fine and logs can be excluded.
[04:49] Sofia Berg: Security question — KMS / key separation. We need to ensure model logs and prompts are encrypted with customer-managed keys.
[04:58] Hannah Park: We can enable customer KMS for log encryption in Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and optional KMIP integrations for enterprise agreements. We'll set a follow-up with your security team.
[05:12] Tomás Alvarez: Back to the canary: what are the exact pass conditions? We need them codified.
[05:19] Avery Chen: Proposed pass conditions: p95 latency delta < +25ms vs baseline, error rate increase < 0.2% absolute, automated quality regression check on a holdout prompt set — no more than 3% increase in bad responses flagged. If any trip, rollout pauses and auto-rolls back.
[05:40] Priya Nair: What's our baseline? Is that current 13b q4 numbers?
[05:46] Luis Moreno: Baseline = your current pilot default (13b q4). We'll capture baseline in staging over a 24h window before the canary.
[05:55] Jake: We also need to test cold-start latency and long session memory retention.
[06:01] Luis Moreno: We'll include cold-start synthetic tests in the A/B run — those are part of the benchmark script.
[06:08] Sofia Berg: Any discussion on quantization artifacts leading to strange token distribution? We observed odd tokenization artifacts in one prompt earlier.
[06:18] Luis Moreno: That's why we recommended the quality holdout set; quant variants can slightly change token choice. If we see content drift we'll either pin FP16 or tune the quantization profile; Redwood Optimize has recommendations and per-workload quant profiles.
[06:34] Priya Nair: If we need to rollback, how quick is rollback? Is it instant?
[06:40] Avery Chen: Rollback is near-instant for routing-level changes — the control plane flips routes and within the SLO for routing it takes seconds. For model compilation changes you might see a warmup which we mitigate with pre-warming options.
[06:55] Tomás Alvarez: Pre-warming — can we pre-warm specific shards for the canary?
[07:01] Luis Moreno: Yes, we can pre-warm a minimal set of workers and KV cache to emulate full load, that reduces first-request jitter. We'll include pre-warm steps in the canary runbook.
[07:13] Priya Nair: What's the expected cost for a 48h A/B run at our traffic? Ballpark.
[07:19] Avery Chen: Based on your average QPS we estimate ~ $2.5k - $4k depending on how much traffic you route to the heavier model. We'll give a precise estimate in the matrix.
[07:30] Sofia Berg: Good. Any competitors in our RFP we should be aware of?
[07:35] Priya Nair: We're also talking to Anthropic for a hosted endpoint, and evaluating OpenAI for a bench baseline. Vertex AI is on the list for enterprise procurement.
[07:46] Avery Chen: OK noted. We'll call out where the differences are in the matrix.
[07:51] Jake: One tiny detail — telemetry tags for each fallback event, can we include the reason (latency vs error vs cost throttle)?
[07:58] Luis Moreno: Yes we'll attach fallback_reason tags and the original primary model id so you can trace.
[08:06] Priya Nair: For the action item owners — we need the updated config to be immutable once pinned for the canary, right?
[08:14] Avery Chen: Correct, pins for canary are immutable during the run. After the 48h window you can publish a new pin.
[08:22] Tomás Alvarez: Ok, let's lock the candidate set: primary = nimble-red-3-35b-q4, fallback = red-chat-3.1-13b-q4, control = red-chat-3.1-13b-q4 (current baseline). Canary split 10% primary / 90% control for first 6 hours then 25/75 for 18 hours then evaluation.
[08:44] Priya Nair: That sounds reasonable. We'll sign off internally if you send the playbook and metrics.
[08:50] Avery Chen: We'll send the matrix, the pilot config (including rollout rules, pre-warm steps, and telemetry hooks) and a runbook for the 48h A/B.
[08:58] Sofia Berg: Also include the KV cache behavior notes and expected replay penalty numbers.
[09:04] Luis Moreno: Noted. One more operational note — if you want private deployment later we can reuse the same pins and rollout specs, just swap the control plane target.
[09:15] Priya Nair: That's helpful for long term. Ok anything else?
[09:20] Hannah Park: I'll schedule the security follow-up with your team and add the KMS checklist.
[09:26] Priya Nair: Great. Thanks everyone.
[09:30] Avery Chen: Thanks team — recap in the next steps and action items, expect the matrix by Thursday.

Outro: call ends ~16:10 PDT.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words removed in places, and some product names approximated (nimble/red-chat internal mapping).
